home.faqTitle: What people ask before their first booking

notHome.q: What if I'm not home when the professional arrives?
notHome.a: You'll get a call and an SMS when they set off, so you know roughly when to expect them. If your plans change, reschedule from the booking screen up to an hour before — there's no charge. If nobody is home and we weren't told, a small visit fee applies to cover the trip.

price.a: Every category has a published rate for common jobs, and you see the estimate before you confirm. If the professional finds the job is bigger than described — a burst pipe rather than a dripping tap — they'll explain why and you approve the revised price before they carry on. Nothing gets added to your bill without your say-so.

cash.a: Yes. Cash on completion is fully supported, alongside eSewa and Khalti. You always pay after the job is done. We never ask for payment in advance, and no professional should ever ask you to send money outside the app.

badWork.q: What if the work isn't done properly?
badWork.a: Report it from the booking within 48 hours and we'll send someone back to put it right at no extra cost. If it still isn't resolved, we refund the job. Repeat complaints affect a professional's trust score, which is why the scores on their profiles are worth reading.

checks.q: How do you check the professionals?
checks.a: Government ID and a citizenship or licence check before anyone takes a job, plus a skills assessment for the trade they're registering in. Their completion rate and rating come from real finished bookings, not self-reported claims.

safety.gas: Don't light a flame or touch any switch — open the windows, close the cylinder valve if you can reach it, and step outside.
safety.burning: Switch off at the mains if you can reach it safely, and don't use that switch or socket again until it has been checked.
safety.liveWire: Switch off at the mains and keep everyone away from the wire until an electrician has been.
safety.unseenPhoto: We couldn't look at your photo just now, so check it yourself: if you can smell gas, or see sparking, scorching or a bare wire, switch off at the mains, don't light a flame, and call us instead of booking.

fallback.generic: We'll match you with the right professional — tell them the details and they'll confirm the price before starting.
fallback.plumbing-emergency: This can cause damage fast, so we'll push you to the front of the queue and send whoever is closest.
fallback.plumbing-leak: Most leaks are a washer or a joint — usually a single visit, and the plumber will carry the parts.
fallback.plumbing-blockage: Blockages get worse if you keep using the fixture. A plumber will clear it and check what caused it.
fallback.plumbing-water: Usually the pump, the inlet valve or an airlock. The plumber will trace it back from the tank.
fallback.electrical-emergency: Treat this as urgent — switch off at the mains if you safely can. We'll dispatch the nearest electrician.
fallback.electrical-fault: An electrician will find whether it's the circuit, the fitting or the supply before quoting anything larger.
fallback.ac-cooling: Weak cooling is usually a dirty filter or low gas. Servicing is cheaper; a refill costs more.
fallback.appliance: The technician diagnoses on site and tells you the part cost before doing any work.
fallback.pest: Priced by the size of the flat and the treatment. Most jobs need one visit plus a follow-up.
fallback.cleaning: Cleaning is booked by hours and flat size, so you'll see the exact price before confirming.
fallback.carpentry: A carpenter will look at whether it's a repair or a replacement, and price the two separately.
fallback.painting: Painting is quoted per square foot after a site visit — the range is wide until someone measures.
fallback.tank: Tanks are priced by capacity. Most households do this twice a year.
fallback.movers: Quoted on distance, floor level and how much you're moving — a survey call settles it in minutes.
